summary: attestation_id_for hashes AttestationDraft, which omits created_by_run, while mint-time idempotence compares created_by_run, so an identical proof minted by a second run is refused as journal damage.
failure_scenario: Two runs sharing one ExecutionManifest (manifest_hash has no run id) mint the same merge/promote draft (subject carries no run; deterministic elapsed_s such as 0.0 from fake clocks). Run A mints att-X with created_by_run=A. Run B's mint_attestation derives the same att-X, _stored_attestation_for_draft builds expected with created_by_run=B, finds stored!=expected and raises JournalDamaged 'already minted with different content'. The run-less policy mint path collides the same way with a run mint. An ordinary identity collision becomes a damage verdict, and the id does not bind 'the attesting run's sealed world' as I2 states.
evidence: Ran a throwaway pytest using tests.run_worlds.create_test_run for run-a and run-b, claim_run each, and mint_attestation(lease, tests.substrate.journal.test_attestation_idempotency._draft()): run-a succeeded, run-b raised JournalDamaged with the message above. Consumer at _sqlite_execution.py:952-975. Not determined whether introduced or pre-existing.

summary: ComponentDef.content_hash excludes labels and lineage but the registry's collision check uses same_definition over the full dump, so provenance-only differences under one identity are reported as JournalDamaged.
failure_scenario: Register a definition, then a second whose behaviour is identical (e.g. a no-op candidate whose ComponentLineage.created_by_run/parent_version or labels differ). content_hash is equal (module docstring says lineage and labels are provenance and do not participate) but same_definition is False, so InMemoryRegistryStore.store_version (registry.py:276) and ComponentRegistry.plan_registration (registry.py:463-468, collision branch) raise JournalDamaged 'already exists with different semantics under the same identity' instead of treating it as the existing version or an ordinary refusal. Damage-class errors for valid input.
evidence: Built c1/c2 ComponentDef differing only in metadata.labels: content_hash equal True, same_definition False; store_version of c1 then c2 raised JournalDamaged 'already stored with a different definition'. plan_registration collision branch read, not executed (needs an importable atomic target).

summary: ArtifactRef.locator, documented as a storage hint that is not identity, participates in ComponentDef.content_hash through LearningProfile.evaluation_dataset.
failure_scenario: Two components whose evaluation_dataset has identical digest/media_type/size but different locator ('file:///a' vs 's3://elsewhere') get different content_hash values, so relocating the dataset mints a new component version identity and a new promotion subject, contradicting envelope.py:5 and :33 ('the digest is the identity, the locator only a storage hint').
evidence: Executed: comp('file:///a').content_hash() != comp('s3://elsewhere').content_hash() -> True (learning payload is model_dump(mode='json') of the profile at component.py:162-164, including the nested locator).

summary: CheckResult._sync_status_and_ok uses Python truthiness on a raw ok before pydantic coercion, so string ok values break the status/ok lockstep.
failure_scenario: model_validate({'name':'n','ok':'false','detail':'','elapsed_s':0.0}) (or ok='0') passes: truthy 'false' makes status='passed', then pydantic coerces ok to False. The model holds status='passed' with ok=False, which the class docstring says cannot happen. When both are supplied, ok='true' with status='passed' is refused ('true' != True) although pydantic would coerce it. The validator also mutates the caller's input dict in place (data['status'] = ...). The downstream attestation lossless check would refuse persisted bytes, but constructors and model_validate paths accept the contradictory value.
evidence: Executed both inputs: status='passed', ok=False. The in-place mutation was read from code, not executed.

summary: digest joins domain and str(schema_version) with NUL without constraining either, so a NUL-bearing domain or non-int version can alias another (domain, version).
failure_scenario: digest('a\0b', 1, p) == digest('a', 'b\x001', p). Reaching it needs a non-int schema_version (violates the annotation) or a NUL in a domain string; with int versions and NUL-free canonical JSON the NUL count differs, so no collision. Defense in depth only.
evidence: Executed: collision True with the str version.

summary: identity.json_value/canonical_json: bool, int and float stay distinct bytes (1, 1.0, true), -0.0 distinct from 0.0, NaN/Infinity and non-str keys and lone surrogates refused; big ints, 1e22, 5e-324 and -0.0 round-trip losslessly through strict JsonValue models (RunResultPreview probe), so validated_run_creation_command's lossless check does not wrongly refuse them.
parse_json_value rejects duplicate keys and non-text input; Digest validator rejects non-lowercase and wrong-length digests.

_sqlite_attestations lossless check (canonical_json of normalized stored object vs model dump) refuses extra fields, coerced scalars and mixed legacy/current check shapes; provenance seals are family-exclusive and the registry refuses m1-m2 provenance for current promotions (_sqlite_registry.py:532).
_sqlite_fact_seals: sealed_fact_hash binds family/key/selector; duplicate or split key/selector rows are refused; inventory is checked in both directions.

_sqlite_commands: JSON null plan/response is treated consistently between SQL (command_plan_exists) and decoder; command id and request hash are re-derived from decoded bytes on read; omitted-vs-null optional fields in resume and domain plans are refused as non-lossless via the wrap serializers.

Tests tests/core/test_identity.py, test_canonical_exchange_coherence.py and test_v6_scalar_collisions.py exercise acceptance and refusal where they target (collision tests reach the guard through real claim/approval flows); test_identity itself has no bool/int/float or -0.0 distinctness case, which test_definition_truths/test_registry_revision cover elsewhere (not run).
